context:
Goal: every page the roadmap links to can be rebuilt from git, as the waiting queue can.
Problem (goal): you are right in part. The export script copies each registered page this account can read into git, which is why the queue rebuilds. These 8 pages live in your other Claude account, so the export cannot read them from here; it must run once while you are signed in there.
Based on (read): the artifact registry on claude-settings main 7b496618 marks all 8 as account other, export false.
Based on (read): the coordinator, 22:21 CST: export_page.py --all copies every registered page into git.
Departs from: the registry, which keeps the 8 as links to pages only your other account can open — c exports them into git, b drops them.

lastAnswer.note: Read 17:48 CST. Sent to the coordinator: it sends you the one export command to run while signed in to the other account; a lane then commits the files and points each link at them. Open until that lands.

options.gain: All 8 rebuild from git, like the waiting queue.
options.how: While signed in to the other account, you run one export command, which the coordinator sends when you pick this; the lane commits the files and points each link at them.
options.label: Run one export in the other account
options.lose: One sign-in to the other account and one command.

options.how: No change: the registry already marks them as other, with no export.
options.label: Keep them as other-account links
options.lose: If that account goes, their content goes with it.

options.gain: No link points at a page this account cannot open.
options.how: The lane removes the 8 links from the roadmap and the registry.
options.label: Drop the links
options.lose: The content is lost to the roadmap.

title: 8 roadmap-linked pages live in your other Claude account, and their content is not in git: export them, or let them go?
why: Recommended: c. One export run while you are signed in to the other account puts all 8 in git.
